content:
STAGE: scope check / design-space scan (metric_ideation_1)
GOAL: pick a hyperbolic SID-table metric that is distinct from Q_H (+0.634 L1), from the two failed ones (hyp_voronoi_margin_l1 -0.081, hyp_adj_r2_l1 +0.156), and from bucket/collision/same-bucket counts.
READ: the task contract and the measured-results list only. No filesystem access in this runtime (import of node:fs rejected); SID/recall artifacts are not inspectable here, so the proposal must be defined on the documented table schema (integer code per item per level, 256 codes, 24587 items) plus the frozen Issue #126 reference and TRAINING split.
OBSERVED: the failed pair are both "spread/margin" style intrinsic-to-embedding quantities (Voronoi margin, adjacency R^2). So the open region of design space is *transition/coverage geometry*: whether the training-time target mass that a source must reach is coverable by a bounded hyperbolic neighbourhood, not how spread out the table is.
REASONING: Recall@10 depends on beam/prefix coverage of plausible targets; a table that puts a source's plausible targets inside a small geodesic ball is coverable, one that scatters them is not. Frame it as coverage of a fixed hyperbolic budget, which is one number and uses only TRAINING pairs.
STILL OPEN: exact formula, derived constants, failure mode, cost.

FINAL: hyp_ref_cone_cov (hyperbolic reference-affinity cone coverage)
Construction: prefix tree of the SID table embedded in the Poincare disk K=-1 via exp_0 with radius ln(1+depth) and recursively equal angular sectors per 256-ary level; hyperbolic distance d_H(u,v)=arcosh(1+2|u-v|^2/((1-|u|^2)(1-|v|^2))). For each TRAIN item q, take A(q)=top-10 items by cosine(s_q,t_j) from the frozen Issue #126 reference; b_q = Karcher (geodesic Frechet) mean of {x_j:j in A(q)} by exp/log fixed point, 10 iters; R_q=max_j d_H(b_q,x_j); g_q=d_H(b_q,0)/(d_H(b_q,0)+R_q); METRIC=mean_q g_q in (0,1], higher better.
Inputs: SID table only + frozen reference reps (cosine ranking) + TRAIN item list. No validation/test pair, no recall, no Stage 3.
Where curvature enters: exp_0 layout (exponential area growth lets the 256-ary tree embed), the arcosh Poincare distance, and the geodesic barycentre (not an arithmetic mean). Ambient-Euclidean versions reorder everything, so not Euclidean in disguise.
Why it tracks recall: Stage 3 retrieves by prefix expansion, so a source is served when the reference's likely targets sit in a small DEEP geodesic cone coverable by beam search. Depth is rewarded only jointly with tightness (scale-free ratio), and max-radius makes one stray neighbour break the source. Adds over Q_H: Q_H scores level-1 prefix ranking alone and is blind to whether a specific source's affinity set is contiguous; A(q) is transition geometry from the reference, not prefix frequency, so it can move while Q_H is flat.
Compute: chunked 24587^2 cosine GEMM ~30 s; ~2e6 2-D log/exp ops <1 s; well under a minute.
Risks: weak/isotropic reference reps -> A(q) ~ random, g_q collapses to a constant; sharp reference -> ceiling effect; equal-sector angles make d_H mostly radial so limited range if depth is nearly constant; Karcher instability for cones across antipodal sectors; O(N^2) cost.
Failure mode: random/hashed code assignment (affinity sets scattered, b_q near origin, R_q large, g_q near floor); also the single-level-1-bucket table with arbitrary suffixes (deep but maximally wide). Best when each source's affinity cone lies inside one fine branch.
Status: complete, no open items. Answer printed in the response.
